quotes.text: This isn't new magic arriving from the cloud. It's redistributed intelligence, specifically Microsoft Graph Data being made slightly more talkative.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: Co-pilot doesn't secretly browse the CEO's mailbox, it's constrained by the same permissions that outlook itself enforces.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: The good news it can only perceive what you can. The bad news, if your permissions are sloppy, it inherits your sloppiness perfectly.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures the permission-inheritance risk of Copilot in one contrast.

takeaways: Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and OneNote draws on Microsoft Graph and can see exactly what the user can see, so sloppy permissions become visible risk.
Sensitivity labels, DLP, retention policies and Purview audit logging must be configured so AI-generated summaries, drafts, charts and slides inherit protection.
Admins should use the Copilot Control System, the AI Administrator role and usage analytics in the Microsoft 365 admin center to govern Copilot before broad rollout.
hook: Copilot is now included in the Microsoft 365 apps people use every day, and it surfaces everything their permissions allow. This episode walks admins and compliance teams through what changes in Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OneNote and which Purview, labeling and admin controls to configure first.
